extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security Briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider:** Azure only.
- **Deployment target:** GitHub Actions workflow named **“Deploy to Azure”**.
- **Triggers:** `push` and `workflow_dispatch`, which means deployments can be initiated automatically on code changes and manually.
- **Runners:** `ubuntu-latest`.
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** No regions, availability zones, or multi-region/multi-AZ topology are shown. Based on the provided data, there is **no explicit high-availability or resilience configuration**.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret store in use:** `github_actions_secret`.
- **Sensitive credential reference:** `principal` is set to `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`.
- **Risk:** The configuration indicates a **GitHub Actions secret-based credential flow** rather than federated identity. No evidence is shown of plaintext secrets in the repository, but the use of a stored credential blob increases exposure risk relative to OIDC federation and requires careful secret handling.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption-at-rest coverage:** `false`.
- **Key management:** No key management mechanism is shown.
- **Implication:** There is **no demonstrated encryption-at-rest coverage** in the supplied configuration. It is not possible to confirm managed key usage, customer-managed keys, or storage-layer encryption controls from the provided data.

### 4) IAM / least-privilege
- **IAM type:** `managed_identity`.
- **Scope:** `subscription`.
- **Trust principal:** `github-actions`.
- **OIDC:** `uses_oidc: false`.
- **Risk:** The identity is scoped at the **subscription** level, which is typically broader than necessary for deployment workflows. No least-privilege role assignment details are provided, so over-permission cannot be confirmed, but the scope is clearly broad. The absence of OIDC means trust is not federated via workload identity; instead, the workflow depends on a stored secret credential.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runner:** `ubuntu-latest` GitHub-hosted runner.
- **Workflow trigger surface:** both event-driven (`push`) and manual (`workflow_dispatch`).
- **OIDC configuration:** disabled (`uses_oidc: false`).
- **Risk:** GitHub-hosted runners are ephemeral, but the use of `ubuntu-latest` introduces some supply-chain variability due to moving image contents. The lack of OIDC is the main CI/CD security gap because long-lived secrets are required for Azure authentication.

### 6) Container security
- No container workload configuration is present in the supplied data.
- Therefore, **root-container status, health checks, and resource limits cannot be assessed** from this evidence.

### 7) Key risks and recommendations
1. **Replace secret-based Azure auth with GitHub OIDC federation.**  
   This removes the need for `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` and reduces secret leakage risk.

2. **Reduce IAM scope from subscription-wide access.**  
   Constrain the Azure identity to the minimum required resource group/resource roles for deployment.

3. **Define explicit resilience and security controls.**  
   Add region/HA intent, verify encryption-at-rest coverage, and document key management settings for all persisted data stores.

relationship_graph_md:
## Component Relationship Graph

- **Entry points:** FastAPI exposes `Login`, `Me`, `Logout`, and `Chat Endpoint`.  
- **Access control:** `Bearer Auth` protects `Chat Endpoint`, `Login`, `Logout`, `Me`, and `Generic` endpoints.  
- **Orchestration:** `OpenAI Agents` calls the `Cancellation`, `FAQ`, `Flight Status`, `Seat Booking`, and `Triage` agents, and also directly calls all listed tools.  
- **Agent routing:** `Triage Agent` delegates to `Flight Status Agent` and `FAQ Agent`.  
- **Model usage:** All five agents use `gpt-4.1-mini`. Both guardrails also use `gpt-4.1-mini`.  
- **Tool access:**  
  - `Triage Agent` can call `Baggage Tool`, `Cancel Flight`, `Display Seat Map`, `Faq Lookup Tool`, and `Flight Status Tool`.  
  - `Cancellation`, `FAQ`, `Flight Status`, and `Seat Booking` agents can each call the same five tools.  
  - `OpenAI Agents` can additionally call `Lookup Reservation` and `Update Seat`.  
- **Guardrails:** `Relevance Guardrail` and `Jailbreak Guardrail` are present, but only their use of `gpt-4.1-mini` is shown; no explicit coverage links to endpoints or tools are shown.  
- **Data stores:** `Sqlite` is present but has **no connections**, so no datastore access is shown.  
- **Notable risk pattern:** Several agents and the framework have broad tool access, including potentially sensitive actions like `Cancel Flight` and `Update Seat`, with no datastore linkage shown.
